reason: The three per-row records of one pass over a Component at rest, each measured alone: the pod buckets by Instance (query.BucketPodsByInstanceIdx, which the plan's observation builds once per pass and the create pass, the promotion and the publication build again), the hold pass (holds.RowsForPlan and holds.Run over every row) and the update selection (every planned Instance read for the roll). Every row is Ready on the spec revision with its pods serving, so nothing moves. The buckets are cut from one array after one count per Instance: 9 / 21 / 7 / 9 allocations at 1,000 and 4,000 single-pod Instances, 160 gangs of eight and 1,725 gangs of two, from 1,022 / 4,048 / 653 / 3,472 with one slice per Instance and the map grown from nothing, and 102 KB / 410 KB / 31 KB / 146 KB from 168 KB / 684 KB / 38 KB / 202 KB. The hold pass reads every row's readings into the pass's one buffer: 15 / 39 / 11 / 15 from 1,014 / 4,038 / 170 / 1,739, and 278 KB / 1.09 MB / 49 KB / 433 KB from 789 KB / 3.14 MB / 130 KB / 1.32 MB, what remains being the pass's rows. The selection writes a line about an Instance only after Enabled says a sink takes it, so the values of a line nobody reads are not copied into interface records: 2,010 / 8,011 / 489 / 3,460 from 7,754 / 31,755 / 1,289 / 13,554, and 43 KB / 163 KB / 32 KB / 127 KB from 366 KB / 1.46 MB / 83 KB / 685 KB, what remains being the two copies of each Instance's runner layout the rolled-set reading makes (ComponentPlan.RunnersFor and ops.rolledSetPods). Re-recorded on 2026-11-06 for the update selection alone, after the debug-line gate: the reading of each Instance already on the target counts the pods of the target's layout without building it (ComponentPlan.TotalPodsFor) and hands an all-member pod list back uncopied (ops.rolledSetPods), two allocations per Instance fewer on every pass: 2,010 to 10 at 1000x1, 8,011 to 11 at 4000x1, 489 to 169 at 160x8 (about one allocation per gang stays, outside the rolled-set reading) and 3,460 to 10 at 1725x2; the pod buckets and the hold pass stand as recorded. Re-recorded with the hold pass's rows pointing into the pass's observation instead of copying each row, 24 bytes a row beside the two maps: the hold-pass bytes 277,808 / 1,092,880 / 48,864 / 433,456 to 89,392 / 355,600 / 13,280 / 113,968 at 1000x1 / 4000x1 / 160x8 / 1725x2; the allocation rows, the pod buckets and the update selection stand as recorded. Two records added beside the three, recorded on the same code: the escalation pass over every row (escalation.Run with nothing to escalate: the planned pod count per Instance built as a map, the pods bucketed once by the caller) at 8 / 20 / 6 / 8 allocations and 21.6 KB / 78.7 KB / 5.0 KB / 21.6 KB at 1000x1 / 4000x1 / 160x8 / 1725x2, and the scale-down scan (workload.ScaleDownExtras, which the plan runs once per pass and the replica pass twice more) at rest, naming no row, at 5 / 17 / 3 / 5 allocations and 19.0 KB / 76.1 KB / 2.3 KB / 19.0 KB, and with a quarter of the rows leaving, naming that quarter, at 8 / 17 / 6 / 11 allocations and 11.5 KB / 50.9 KB / 2.8 KB / 23.1 KB. Each of the three builds its own set of the plan's Instances by index on every call; the hold pass builds two more (holds.RowsForPlan).
